title: Primary 2 Time: Telling Time, am and pm, Hours and Minutes
seo_title: P2 Time Worksheets: Free Primary 2 Maths on Telling Time, Hours and Minutes with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Telling time to the minute; measuring time in hours and minutes; converting hours and minutes
meta_desc: Free P2 maths practice on time: read clocks to the minute, am and pm, how long, and changing h and min. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: 1 h 20 min = 60 + 20 = 80 min, and 80 min = 1 h 20 min.
body_html:
The two hands

A clock has two hands. The short hour hand shows the hour. The long minute hand shows the minutes. Each number is 5 min for the minute hand, so count in 5s. Between two numbers there are 5 small marks. Each small mark is 1 min.

Read the clock

The hour hand is between 9 and 10. The minute hand points to 4.

The hour is 9. Count in 5s to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20.

Answer: 9.20

am and pm

am: from 12 midnight to 12 noon (night and morning). pm: from 12 noon to 12 midnight (afternoon and evening).

What happensTime
Wake up for school6.15 am
Recess9.40 am
Lunch12.30 pm
Dinner7.20 pm

How long?

1 h = 60 min, not 100 min. Count on to the next o’clock first, then on to the end time.

Find the end time

A show starts at 7.00 pm. It lasts 1 h 30 min. When does it end?

Add 1 h: 8.00 pm. Add 30 min: 8.30 pm.

Answer: 8.30 pm

Change hours and minutes

Hours and minutesMinutes
1 h60 min
1 h 20 min60 + 20 = 80 min
2 h120 min
2 h 15 min120 + 15 = 135 min

To change minutes to hours and minutes, take out groups of 60 min.

Minutes to h and min

Change 80 min to hours and minutes.

80 = 60 + 20. 60 min is 1 h, and 20 min is left.

Answer: 1 h 20 min

Word problems with a model

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Hour hand read as the minutes: 3.45 read as 9.15The short hand is the hour. The long hand is the minutes
Minute hand on 4 read as 4 minEach number is 5 min: 4 × 5 = 20 min
Hour hand just before 5 read as 5It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is still 4
1 h = 100 min: 11.15 − 10.40 = 75 min1 h = 60 min. Count on: 20 + 15 = 35 min
80 min = 1 h 80 minTake out 60 min: 80 − 60 = 20. 80 min = 1 h 20 min
Breakfast at 7.00 pmMorning times are am: 7.00 am

faq.q: What is taught in P2 time?
faq.a: In Primary 2, students tell time to the minute, use am and pm, find how long something takes in hours and minutes, and change hours and minutes to minutes and back.

faq.q: How do I change hours and minutes into minutes?
faq.a: Change each hour to 60 min, then add the minutes. For example, 1 h 20 min = 60 + 20 = 80 min.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in P2 time?
faq.a: The most common mistake is treating 1 h as 100 min, for example writing 80 min as 1 h 80 min or working out 11.15 − 10.40 as 75 min. Remind your child that 1 h is 60 min.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Telling time, measuring time in hours and minutes and converting hours and minutes are part of Measurement in the MOE 2021 Primary 2 Mathematics Syllabus (Standard Mathematics).

sets.title: Read the clock: to 5 minutes and to the minute

items.q: The minute hand moves from one number to the next number. How many minutes is that?
items.e: There are 5 small marks between two numbers. Each small mark is 1 minute. So one number to the next is 5 min. That is why we count in 5s.

items.q: The minute hand points to 7. How many minutes past the hour is it?
items.e: Count in 5s from the 12 to the 7: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. It is 35 min past the hour. (Not 7 min: the number is not the minutes.)

The minute hand (long) points to 12, so it is exactly 1 o’clock. So the time is 1.00. (Not 12.05: that reads the hour hand as the minutes. Not 1.12: when the minute hand points to 12, it is 0 minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The minute hand (long) points to 4. Count in 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 min. So the time is 2.20. (Not 2.04: each number is 5 minutes, so 4 means 4 × 5 = 20. Not 4.10: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 3 and 4. It has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is 3. The minute hand (long) points to 7. Count in 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 min. So the time is 3.35. (Not 4.35: the hour hand is before 4, so it is not 4 o’clock yet. Not 7.15: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The minute hand (long) points to 2. Count in 5s: 2 × 5 = 10 min. So the time is 1.10. (Not 1.02: each number is 5 minutes, so 2 means 2 × 5 = 10. Not 2.05: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The minute hand (long) points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 min. So the time is 8.50. (Not 9.50: the hour hand is before 9, so it is not 9 o’clock yet. Not 10.40: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 11 and 12. It has not reached 12 yet, so the hour is 11. The minute hand (long) points to 5. Count in 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 min. So the time is 11.25. (Not 11.05: each number is 5 minutes, so 5 means 5 × 5 = 25. Not 5.55: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 10 and 11. It has not reached 11 yet, so the hour is 10. The minute hand (long) points to 9. Count in 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 min. So the time is 10.45. (Not 11.45: the hour hand is before 11, so it is not 11 o’clock yet. Not 9.50: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

The hour hand (short) is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The minute hand (long) points to 11. Count in 5s: 11 × 5 = 55 min. So the time is 2.55. (Not 3.55: the hour hand is before 3, so it is not 3 o’clock yet. Not 11.10: that reads the hour hand as the minutes.)

items.q: The hour hand is between 3 and 4. The minute hand points to 9. What time is it?
items.e: The hour hand has not reached 4, so the hour is 3. Count in 5s to the 9: 9 × 5 = 45. It is 3.45. (9.15 swaps the hands. 3.09 forgets to count in 5s.)

The hour hand (short) is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The minute hand (long) is 1 small mark past the 2. Count in 5s to 10, then in 1s: 11 min. So the time is 9.11. (Not 9.10: count the small marks after the 2 too.)

The hour hand (short) is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The minute hand (long) is 1 small mark past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then in 1s: 16 min. So the time is 4.16. (Not 4.15: count the small marks after the 3 too.)

The hour hand (short) is between 2 and 3. It has not reached 3 yet, so the hour is 2. The minute hand (long) is 1 small mark past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then in 1s: 36 min. So the time is 2.36. (Not 3.36: the hour hand has not reached 3 yet.)

The hour hand (short) is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The minute hand (long) is 3 small marks past the 10. Count in 5s to 50, then in 1s: 53 min. So the time is 7.53. (Not 8.53: the hour hand has not reached 8 yet.)

The hour hand (short) is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The minute hand (long) is 3 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then in 1s: 18 min. So the time is 4.18. (Not 4.15: count the small marks after the 3 too.)

The hour hand (short) is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The minute hand (long) is 1 small mark past the 8. Count in 5s to 40, then in 1s: 41 min. So the time is 12.41. (Not 1.41: the hour hand has not reached 1 yet.)

The hour hand (short) is between 8 and 9. It has not reached 9 yet, so the hour is 8. The minute hand (long) is 3 small marks past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then in 1s: 48 min. So the time is 8.48. (Not 9.48: the hour hand has not reached 9 yet.)

At 5.38 the minute hand is 3 small marks past the 7 (count in 5s to 35, then in 1s to 38), and the hour hand is between 5 and 6. That is clock C. (Clock A shows 6.38; clock B shows 5.22; clock D shows 5.07.)

At 8.13 the minute hand is 3 small marks past the 2 (count in 5s to 10, then in 1s to 13), and the hour hand is between 8 and 9. That is clock B. (Clock A shows 9.13; clock C shows 8.47; clock D shows 8.02.)

items.q: When do we use am?
items.e: am times go from 12 midnight to 12 noon: the night and the morning. pm times go from 12 noon to 12 midnight: the afternoon and the evening.

items.q: When do we use pm?
items.e: pm times go from 12 noon to 12 midnight: the afternoon and the evening.

items.q: What is 12 noon?
items.e: 12 noon is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day. 12 o’clock at night is 12 midnight.

items.q: Which is the best time for breakfast?
items.e: Breakfast is in the morning. Morning times are am. So 7.00 am is the best time. (1.00 am is in the middle of the night.)

items.q: Which is the best time for lunch?
items.e: Lunch is just after 12 noon. Times after 12 noon are pm. So 12.30 pm is the best time. (12.30 am is just after 12 midnight.)

items.q: Which time is in the afternoon?
items.e: The afternoon comes after 12 noon, so it is a pm time: 3.15 pm. (3.15 am is in the night.)

The hour hand (short) is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The minute hand (long) points to 1. Count in 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 min. The clock shows 6.05. This happens in the morning, so it is 6.05 am. (Not 6.05 pm.)

The hour hand (short) is between 6 and 7. It has not reached 7 yet, so the hour is 6. The minute hand (long) points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 min. The clock shows 6.50. This happens in the morning, so it is 6.50 am. (Not 6.50 pm.)

The hour hand (short) is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The minute hand (long) points to 6. Count in 5s: 6 × 5 = 30 min. The clock shows 9.30. This happens in the morning, so it is 9.30 am. (Not 9.30 pm.)

items.q: What is Sarah most likely doing at 3.00 am?
items.e: 3.00 am is 3 hours after 12 midnight. It is the middle of the night, so Sarah is most likely sleeping.

The hour hand (short) is between 12 and 1. It has not reached 1 yet, so the hour is 12. The minute hand (long) points to 5. Count in 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 min. The clock shows 12.25. This happens just after 12 noon, so it is 12.25 pm. (Not 12.25 am.)

items.q: Which comes 1 minute after 11.59 am?
items.e: 11.59 am is in the morning, 1 minute before 12 o’clock. The next minute is 12 noon. (12 midnight comes 1 minute after 11.59 pm.)

The hour hand (short) is between 1 and 2. It has not reached 2 yet, so the hour is 1. The minute hand (long) points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 min. The clock shows 1.50. This happens in the afternoon, so it is 1.50 pm. (Not 1.50 am.)

The hour hand (short) is between 4 and 5. It has not reached 5 yet, so the hour is 4. The minute hand (long) points to 9. Count in 5s: 9 × 5 = 45 min. The clock shows 4.45. This happens in the afternoon, so it is 4.45 pm. (Not 4.45 am.)

The hour hand (short) is between 7 and 8. It has not reached 8 yet, so the hour is 7. The minute hand (long) points to 5. Count in 5s: 5 × 5 = 25 min. The clock shows 7.25. This happens in the evening, so it is 7.25 pm. (Not 7.25 am.)

items.q: Which is the best time for going to bed?
items.e: Children go to bed in the evening. Evening times are pm. So 8.45 pm is the best time. (1.30 pm is just after lunch.)

The hour hand (short) is between 9 and 10. It has not reached 10 yet, so the hour is 9. The minute hand (long) points to 1. Count in 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 min. The clock shows 9.05. This happens in the evening, so it is 9.05 pm. (Not 9.05 am.)

items.q: It is 11.00 am. What time is it 2 hours later?
items.e: Count on 2 hours: 11.00 am → 12 noon → 1.00 pm. After 12 noon, am changes to pm. (9.00 am is 2 hours earlier. 12 noon is only 1 hour later.)

items.q: It is 10.30 pm. What time is it 2 hours later?
items.e: Count on 2 hours: 10.30 pm → 11.30 pm → 12.30. We passed 12 midnight, so pm changes to am: 12.30 am. (12.30 pm is in the day, after lunch time.)

items.q: Put these times in order, earliest first.
items.e: Morning (am) comes first, then 12 noon, then the afternoon (pm). So the order is 9.00 am, 12 noon, 2.00 pm.

items.q: The minute hand goes all the way round, from 12 back to 12. How long is that?
items.e: The minute hand passes 12 numbers. Each number is 5 min: 12 × 5 = 60 min. 60 min = 1 h. (1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: The minute hand moves from 12 to 6. How long is that?
items.e: From 12 to 6 is 6 jumps of 5 min: 6 × 5 = 30 min. That is half an hour.

items.q: The minute hand moves from 2 to 5. How long is that?
items.e: From 2 to 5 is 3 jumps: 3, 4, 5. Each jump is 5 min: 3 × 5 = 15 min. (Not 3 min: each jump is 5 minutes.)

items.q: The hour hand moves from 2 to 5. How long is that?
items.e: The hour hand moves 1 number every hour. From 2 to 5 is 3 jumps, so it is 3 h. (15 min is for the minute hand. 3 min reads the hours as minutes. 7 h adds 2 and 5.)

items.q: Which takes about 1 h?
items.e: Brushing your teeth and tying your shoelaces take a few minutes. A night’s sleep takes many hours. A swimming lesson takes about 1 h.

items.q: Recess is about 30 ___. Choose the unit.
items.e: Recess is short, so we use minutes. Recess is about 30 min. (30 h is more than a whole day.)

items.q: A movie at the cinema lasts about 2 ___. Choose the unit.
items.e: 2 min is far too short, and 2 days is far too long. A movie lasts about 2 h.

Both times are in the same hour. The minute hand moves from 20 min to 55 min: 55 − 20 = 35 min. (75 min adds 20 and 55 instead of taking away. Not 7 min: the hand moves 7 numbers, from 4 to 11, and each number is 5 min.)
Both times are in the same hour. 50 − 25 = 25 min. (75 min adds the minutes instead of taking away. 5 min counts the numbers, not the minutes.)

items.q: A maths lesson starts at 8.05 am and ends at 8.45 am. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 min. (Not 45 min: the lesson starts at 8.05, not at 8.00. 50 min adds 5 and 45 instead of taking away.)
Count the jumps of the hour hand, not the numbers: 9 → 10 → 11. That is 2 jumps, so it is 2 h. (3 h counts the numbers 9, 10 and 11. 200 min counts 1 h as 100 min.)

items.q: A party starts at 1.00 pm and ends at 4.00 pm. How long is the party?
items.e: Count on: 1.00 pm → 2.00 pm → 3.00 pm → 4.00 pm. That is 3 jumps: 3 h. (3 min uses the wrong unit. 4 h counts the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. 300 min counts 1 h as 100 min.)

items.q: A show starts at 10.30 am and ends at 11.30 am. How long is the show?
items.e: The minutes are the same (30), and the hour goes up by 1. So it is 1 h. (Not 100 min: 1 h is 60 min. 2 h counts the numbers 10 and 11.)

items.q: A lesson starts at 10.40 am and ends at 11.15 am. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 10.40 am to 11.00 am is 20 min. Then 11.00 am to 11.15 am is 15 min. 20 + 15 = 35 min. (Not 75 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Xin Yi goes on a bus ride from 2.50 pm to 3.20 pm. How long is the ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 2.50 pm to 3.00 pm is 10 min. Then 3.00 pm to 3.20 pm is 20 min. 10 + 20 = 30 min. (Not 70 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Priya plays in the playground from 11.45 am to 12.10 pm. How long does she play?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 11.45 am to 12 noon is 15 min. Then 12 noon to 12.10 pm is 10 min. 15 + 10 = 25 min. (Not 65 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A cooking class starts at 4.00 pm and ends at 5.25 pm. How long is the class?
items.e: 4.00 pm to 5.00 pm is 1 h. 5.00 pm to 5.25 pm is 25 min. So it is 1 h 25 min. (Not 125 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: A swimming lesson is from 9.30 am to 11.00 am. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 9.30 am to 10.00 am is 30 min. Then 10.00 am to 11.00 am is 1 h. 30 min + 1 h = 1 h 30 min. (Not 170 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min, so do not just take away the numbers.)

Count on to the next o’clock first: 4.25 pm to 5.00 pm is 35 min. Then 5.00 pm to 5.40 pm is 40 min. 35 + 40 = 75 min = 1 h 15 min. (Not 115 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Farah visits the library from 1.35 pm to 3.05 pm. How long is her visit?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 1.35 pm to 2.00 pm is 25 min. Then 2.00 pm to 3.05 pm is 1 h 5 min. 25 min + 1 h 5 min = 1 h 30 min. (Not 170 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: 1 h = ☐ min. What is the missing number?
items.e: The minute hand goes round once in 1 h: 12 × 5 = 60. So 1 h = 60 min. (Not 100.)

items.q: Half an hour = ☐ min. What is the missing number?
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. Half of 60 is 30. (Not 50: 1 h is not 100 min.)

items.q: 2 h = ☐ min. What is the missing number?
items.e: 2 h = 60 min + 60 min = 120 min. (Not 200: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: 3 h = ☐ min. What is the missing number?
Change 1 h 20 min to minutes.
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 60 min + 20 min = 80 min. (Not 120 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 1 h 45 min to minutes.
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 60 min + 45 min = 105 min. (Not 145 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 1 h 5 min to minutes.
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 60 min + 5 min = 65 min. (Not 105 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 80 min to hours and minutes.
items.e: Take out groups of 60 min. 80 = 60 + 20. Each 60 min is 1 h. So 80 min = 1 h 20 min. (Not 1 h 80 min: after taking out 1 h, only 20 min is left.)

items.q: Change 75 min to hours and minutes.
items.e: Take out groups of 60 min. 75 = 60 + 15. Each 60 min is 1 h. So 75 min = 1 h 15 min. (Not 1 h 75 min: after taking out 1 h, only 15 min is left.)

items.q: Change 90 min to hours and minutes.
items.e: Take out groups of 60 min. 90 = 60 + 30. Each 60 min is 1 h. So 90 min = 1 h 30 min. (Not 1 h 90 min: after taking out 1 h, only 30 min is left.)

items.q: 100 min = 1 h ☐ min. What is the missing number?
items.e: Take 60 min out of 100 min to make 1 h: 100 − 60 = 40. So 100 min = 1 h 40 min. (Not 0: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 2 h 10 min to minutes.
items.e: 2 h = 2 × 60 min = 120 min. 120 min + 10 min = 130 min. (Not 210 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 2 h 35 min to minutes.
items.e: 2 h = 2 × 60 min = 120 min. 120 min + 35 min = 155 min. (Not 235 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 3 h 15 min to minutes.
items.e: 3 h = 3 × 60 min = 180 min. 180 min + 15 min = 195 min. (Not 315 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 110 min to hours and minutes.
items.e: Take out groups of 60 min. 110 = 60 + 50. Each 60 min is 1 h. So 110 min = 1 h 50 min. (Not 1 h 110 min: after taking out 1 h, only 50 min is left. Not 1 h 10 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 135 min to hours and minutes.
items.e: Take out groups of 60 min. 135 = 60 + 60 + 15. Each 60 min is 1 h. So 135 min = 2 h 15 min. (Not 1 h 35 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Change 150 min to hours and minutes.
items.e: Take out groups of 60 min. 150 = 60 + 60 + 30. Each 60 min is 1 h. So 150 min = 2 h 30 min. (Not 1 h 50 min: 1 h is 60 min, not 100 min.)

items.q: Which is longer: 1 h 10 min or 75 min?
items.e: Change 1 h 10 min to minutes: 60 + 10 = 70 min. 75 min is more than 70 min, so 75 min is longer. (1 h 10 min is not 110 min.)

items.q: Which is longer: 1 h 30 min or 90 min?
items.e: Change 1 h 30 min to minutes: 60 + 30 = 90 min. So they are the same.

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: Change them all to minutes: 1 h 15 min = 75 min, 1 h = 60 min, 1 h 5 min = 65 min. 75 is the most, so 1 h 15 min is the longest.

items.q: Ryan starts his homework at 3.15 pm. He takes 30 min. When does he finish?
items.e: Count on 30 min from 3.15 pm: 15 + 30 = 45. He finishes at 3.45 pm. (4.15 pm is 1 h later. 2.45 pm is 30 min earlier.)

items.q: Recess lasts 30 min. It ends at 10.00 am. When does recess start?
items.e: Count back 30 min from 10.00 am: 9.30 am. (10.30 am is 30 min after recess ends.)

items.q: School ends at 1.30 pm. Hui Min reaches home 40 min later. When does she reach home?
items.e: From 1.30 pm, 30 min takes you to 2.00 pm. 40 − 30 = 10 more minutes makes 2.10 pm. (2.30 pm is 1 h later, not 40 min.)

items.q: A National Day concert at the void deck starts at 7.00 pm. It lasts 1 h 30 min. When does it end?
items.e: Add 1 h: 7.00 pm → 8.00 pm. Add 30 min: 8.30 pm. The concert ends at 8.30 pm. (7.30 pm forgets the 1 h. 8.00 pm forgets the 30 min.)

items.q: Arjun reads for 25 min in the morning and 40 min at night. How long does he read altogether? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
items.e: 25 min + 40 min = 65 min. 65 min = 60 min + 5 min = 1 h 5 min. (Not 1 h 65 min: after taking out 1 h, only 5 min is left. Not 6 h 5 min: 65 is 65 minutes, not 6 hours.)

items.q: A train ride and a bus ride take 1 h altogether. The train ride takes 35 min. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 60 min − 35 min = 25 min. (65 min works out 100 − 35, as if 1 h were 100 min.)

items.q: Chloe’s swimming lesson is 1 h. Wei Ming’s lesson is 15 min shorter. How long is Wei Ming’s lesson?
items.e: 1 h = 60 min. 60 min − 15 min = 45 min. (85 min works out 100 − 15, as if 1 h were 100 min. 1 h 15 min adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: Mrs Lim’s cake needs 45 min in the oven. It is ready at 4.00 pm. When did she put it in the oven?
items.e: Count back 45 min from 4.00 pm. 4.00 pm − 1 h = 3.00 pm, so 45 min back is 15 min after 3.00 pm: 3.15 pm. (3.55 pm works out 400 − 45 = 355, as if 1 h were 100 min. 4.45 pm counts forwards.)

items.q: Zhi Hao practises the piano for 50 min. Ethan practises for 20 min longer. How long does Ethan practise? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
items.e: 50 min + 20 min = 70 min. 70 min = 60 min + 10 min = 1 h 10 min. (Not 1 h 70 min: after taking out 1 h, only 10 min is left. 30 min takes away instead of adding.)

items.q: Primary 2 students visit the Singapore Zoo from 9.30 am to 12.30 pm. How long is the visit?
items.e: Count the jumps: 9.30 am → 10.30 am → 11.30 am → 12.30 pm. That is 3 jumps of 1 h, so the visit is 3 h. (4 h counts the numbers 9, 10, 11 and 12. 300 min counts 1 h as 100 min.)

items.q: Mdm Wong’s flight leaves Changi Airport at 10.45 am. The flight takes 2 h. What time is it in Singapore when the flight lands?
items.e: Count on 2 h: 10.45 am → 11.45 am → 12.45. We passed 12 noon, so it is 12.45 pm. (12.45 am would be after 12 midnight.)

items.q: Sarah spends 1 h 15 min at Gardens by the Bay. Jun Jie spends 20 min longer there. How long does Jun Jie spend there?
items.e: 1 h 15 min + 20 min: add the minutes, 15 + 20 = 35. So it is 1 h 35 min. (55 min takes away instead of adding. 35 min forgets the 1 h.)

items.q: Mei Ling watches TV for 1 h 20 min. Nurul watches TV for 55 min. How much longer does Mei Ling watch TV?
items.e: Change 1 h 20 min to minutes: 60 + 20 = 80 min. 80 min − 55 min = 25 min. (65 min works out 120 − 55, as if 1 h were 100 min. 2 h 15 min adds the two times.)

items.q: Sports Day starts at 8.00 am and ends at 11.30 am. How long is Sports Day?
items.e: 8.00 am to 11.00 am is 3 h. 11.00 am to 11.30 am is 30 min. So Sports Day is 3 h 30 min. (330 min works out 1130 − 800, as if 1 h were 100 min.)
4.30 pm to 5.00 pm is 30 min. 5.00 pm to 6.00 pm is 1 h. So it is 1 h 30 min. (170 min works out 600 − 430, as if 1 h were 100 min.)

items.q: Raju’s family leaves home at 8.50 am. They reach Sentosa at 9.35 am. How long is the trip?
items.e: 8.50 am to 9.00 am is 10 min. 9.00 am to 9.35 am is 35 min. 10 + 35 = 45 min. (85 min works out 935 − 850, as if 1 h were 100 min.)

items.q: Kumar practises his spelling for 20 min each day for 4 days. How long does he practise altogether? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
items.e: 4 units = 4 × 20 min = 80 min. 80 min = 60 min + 20 min = 1 h 20 min. (Not 1 h 80 min: after taking out 1 h, only 20 min is left. Not 24 min: 20 + 4 adds instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Ahmad leaves home at 9.40 am. He takes the MRT for 35 min. Then he walks for 10 min to the library. When does he reach the library?
items.e: The trip takes 35 min + 10 min = 45 min. From 9.40 am, 20 min takes you to 10.00 am. 45 − 20 = 25 more minutes makes 10.25 am. (10.15 am forgets the 10-min walk.)

items.q: A Chinese New Year concert has two parts of 45 min each, with a 15 min break in between. How long is the whole concert?
items.e: 45 + 15 + 45 = 105 min. 105 min = 60 min + 45 min = 1 h 45 min. (1 h 5 min counts 1 h as 100 min. 60 min forgets the second part.)

items.q: Hafiz goes to bed at 9.00 pm. He wakes up at 6.00 am the next morning. How long does he sleep?
items.e: 9.00 pm to 12 midnight is 3 h. 12 midnight to 6.00 am is 6 h. 3 h + 6 h = 9 h. (3 h works out 9 − 6. 15 h adds 9 and 6.)
